s01.text: Here is the third term in the training bill: activations.

s02.text: Every layer passes its output to the next one, and the backward pass needs those outputs to work out the gradients.

s03.text: So you keep them. All of them. For every layer, for every token in the batch.

s04.text: And activations are the only term that does not scale with the model. They scale with batch size and sequence length.

s05.text: Double the sequence length and you double the activation memory.

s06.text: Which means the term you can control without touching the model is the one that scales with your batch size.

s07.text: There is a trade available. Do not save the activations. Save only the inputs to a few checkpoints.

s08.text: Then when the backward pass needs a layer you threw away, recompute it from the last checkpoint.

s09.text: You traded memory for arithmetic. And arithmetic is the thing a data centre actually has.

s10.text: The cost is real. A checkpointed step does about a third more work than an uncheckpointed one.

s11.text: A third more compute to fit twice the batch, or twice the context.

s12.text: Which is why nobody turns it on for its own sake. You turn it on when the run will not fit.

s13.text: Throw it away. Compute it again. That is the whole trick.
